title: Permutation invariance of a product distribution
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinate indices. For every function $x$ from those indices to $\Omega$, the product distribution of $n$ independent samples from $\pi$ assigns the same mass to $x$ and to the function whose $i$th coordinate is $x(\sigma(i))$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\sigma$ is a permutation of the $n$ coordinate indices
$x$ is a function from the coordinate indices to $\Omega$
